post.summary: Analyze text readability and linguistic complexity
post.description: Calculates classic English readability metrics (Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, Gunning Fog Index, Coleman-Liau, and ARI) alongside structural statistics and reliability assessments.

post.summary: Identify the language of submitted text
post.description: Uses character n-gram rank-order profiling (Cavnar & Trenkle, 1994) to estimate the most likely language of the input text. Supports: English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Polish, Russian, Arabic, Chinese, and Japanese.

post.summary: Extract TF-IDF keyphrases from a corpus of review texts
post.description: Applies Term Frequency–Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) to a submitted corpus of documents and returns ranked keyphrases for each document (or a single focus document). IDF is computed from the submitted corpus; no external data or pre-trained model is used. Supports unigrams and bigrams. Scores are purely statistical and do not represent semantic meaning.

post.summary: Analyze sentiment polarity and aspect-level sentiment for a review
post.description: Performs rule- and lexicon-based sentiment analysis on a consumer review text. Calculates compound polarity [-1.0 to +1.0], positive/negative/neutral proportions, and extracts polar highlight tokens with negation, booster, and clause modifiers. Optionally extracts targeted sentiment for specific product aspects.

TopicsRequest.title: TopicsRequest
TopicsRequest.description:
Input payload for TF-IDF keyphrase extraction.

Provide a ``documents`` list (corpus). To surface keyphrases for a single
document relative to the rest of the corpus, set ``focus_index`` to that
document's 0-based position.

TF-IDF requires a corpus to compute inverse document frequencies. Submitting
a single document without any reference corpus makes IDF degenerate (all
terms receive equal weight); the response will include a warning in
``limitations``.
